newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee perks up on talk of Folger price hike.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee perks up on talk of Folger price hike.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures rose sharply this morning on widespread talk that leading roaster Folgers will raise its retail prices, market sources said.

Although a Folgers spokeswoman was unavailable for comment and other Folgers employees could not confirm the talk, traders said the Procter & Gamble unit will raise the list price on its standard 13-ounce can by 20 cents, effective immediately.
"It's what everyone is talking about on the floor," one trader said. "The buying came in reaction to the news about Folgers."
At 1018 EDT, July futures were up 3.85 cents at 200.25 cents a lb, traded 201.00 to 196.00 cents. Spot May was 4.25 higher at 224.50, while the rest gained 0.50 to 2.90 cents.
Folgers last announced a price increase on March 10, when it raised the list price on its standard 13-ounce can by 15 cents due to higher prices of green coffee on the world's futures markets.
The increase, which came only a week after a 45-cent price hike, brought the price for a standard can to $2.86.

Industry sources said another rise in retail prices was to be expected after the continuing upswing in coffee futures amid low inventories at roasting plants and the prospect of smaller harvests in many Latin American countries.
"I'm not surprised that Folgers would raise its prices because the market has been so strong," one trader said. "And I bet we are going to see more roasters raise their prices."
After breaching the $2 mark, traders said July's next upside hurdle was seen at 203.50 cents, a life-of-contract high set Friday. Support at today's low of 196.00 cents.
